Is the daughter's begging over the smartphone the thing that reveals she is in the kidnapper's vicinity—i.e., is the daughter actually with the kidnapper, so the father refuses because paying would leave her at the kidnapper's mercy?

text: The father is himself the hostage. The kidnapper is with him and has the daughter on the smartphone: she begs for a life to be spared, while the kidnapper shouts the demand—100 million yen, alone, by noon tomorrow, no police. Because the father is the captive, he knows the money cannot save him: the kidnapper is with him and will kill the hostage regardless of payment. He also knows the only person who could raise and deliver the ransom is his daughter, and the kidnapper insists she bring it "alone," without police or anyone to protect her. Complying would therefore not rescue the father; it would only enrich a killer and force his daughter to walk unaccompanied into danger, since both father and daughter confirmed that her coming alone would put her at the kidnapper's mercy. That threat to his daughter—rather than any willingness or ability to pay—is what makes the father decide the ransom should not be paid. His refusal is meant to keep his daughter out of the trap the kidnapper has set.
